- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.3) over 3+ days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract pessimism.
- Model frequently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.0% to initial forecast values.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags; delay upward adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10+ consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until trend stabilizes.
